title: edikt governance sidecar
description: The <artifact>.edikt.yaml sidecar file co-located next to a governance artifact — ADR, invariant, or guideline. As of v0.6.0 it replaces the in-body [edikt:directives:start]/[edikt:directives:end] sentinel block; compile reads sidecars verbatim and never mutates the parent .md. The PRD and SPEC sidecars (prd-sidecar.v1.schema.json, spec-sidecar.v1.schema.json) cover their own artifact classes.
$comment: v1.1 (additive) — paths, scope, prohibitions are optional. KnownFields(true) in the Go decoder makes the v1.1 fields forward-only: a v1.0 reader cannot parse a sidecar that uses them. edikt distributes as a single binary; upgrade as a unit. The schema version stays at 1 because the on-disk shape only widens.

schema_version.description: Sidecar schema version. The governance sidecar uses a discrete integer (1) because its on-disk shape is a v1-or-v2 contract, not a semver-versioned one — bump only when the on-disk shape changes in a way that older readers cannot interpret. PRD/SPEC sidecars (prd-sidecar.v1.schema.json, spec-sidecar.v1.schema.json) deliberately use a string semver ("1.0") for additive evolution within v1.x; the asymmetry is intentional. v0.6.0 ships with version 1.

topic.description: Kebab-case topic identifier used to group directives across artifacts during compile. 1–40 characters, must start with a lowercase letter, may contain lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.

path.description: Relative path (from the project root) to the parent .md artifact this sidecar describes. Validated by /edikt:doctor — a sidecar whose path doesn't resolve is reported as orphaned.

body_digest.description: Hex SHA-256 of the parent .md body after whitespace normalization, recorded at extraction time (ADR-053). Powers the BODY DRIFT signal: when this differs from the recomputed digest, prose changed that extraction never saw, so the sidecar may be INCOMPLETE — distinct from ANCHOR DRIFT, where a recorded quote no longer matches and the sidecar is WRONG. This is NOT the source_hash that ADR-027 forbids: that field was a fast-path substitute for checking, where a divergence between recorded and computed values was the DEFECT. Here divergence is the PRODUCT — the field exists precisely to be compared and to disagree. source_hash, agent_prompt_version and directives_hash remain forbidden. Optional: sidecars written before ADR-053 have no baseline and MUST be reported as UNMEASURED, never as unchanged.

items.description: Lowercase signal phrase. Indexed for search and for the benchmark attack corpus; topic routing is the approved registry description, not this set when a task matches the signal.

signals.description: Lowercase, deduplicated keyword/phrase signals that route work to this artifact.

paths.description: v1.1 (optional). File-glob patterns scoping where this artifact's directives apply (e.g. 'tools/edikt/**/*.go', 'templates/hooks/**/*.sh'). Glob syntax is doublestar/v4 compatible. Validated as non-empty strings at parse time; full glob-syntax validation deferred to gov:compile.

scope.description: v1.1 (optional). Lifecycle phases during which this artifact's directives are surfaced. Closed enum: planning | design | implementation | review. ADR Decision blocks default to [design, implementation, review]; INV Statements default to [implementation, review]; ADR architectural prohibitions default to [planning, design, review].

text.description: MUST NOT directive synthesised from a rejected option. Same shape as directives[].text.

derived_from.description: Provenance hint for the prohibition (e.g., 'rejected_option_b'). Optional; auditability only — not used by compile.

verify.description: Optional shell command that returns exit 0 when the prohibition is honored, non-zero when it is violated. Run via `bin/edikt verify gov <ID>`. The completion-evidence discipline refuses to declare success when any verify fails. Omit when no mechanical check is possible — the field stays absent, not empty.

verify_kind.description: v1.2 (optional). The enforcement medium of the verify command. behavioral = runs code and asserts a property; tooling = invokes a stable external tool with a fixed rule ID; structural = grep/file-presence over content (only valid when the prohibition's property is itself structural). Layer-independent — applies to every verify: command regardless of which sidecar carries it.

intent.description: v1.2 (optional). One-line semantic claim of the prohibition, generator-neutral. Consumed by the L2 governance-verifier instead of the raw text. Must read as the assertion without referencing implementation symbols the generator controls.

falsifying_observation.description: v1.2 (optional). One-line description of what a violation looks like. Used by the L2 verifier to decide PASS/FAIL/NEEDS_REVIEW. Required (non-null) when verify_kind == behavioral; Phase B compile enforces this conditional-required constraint.

human_approved_at.description: v1.2 (optional). RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of human approval. Required by CONTRACT (non-null) for verify_kind == behavioral per ADR-036 §2, but NOT enforced at compile — the check is deferred to SPEC-009 Plan B (AC-4.3), so an unapproved behavioral verify compiles today. Set by `bin/edikt sidecar approve`.

positive_fixture_path.description: Path to a script that exits 0 when the directive's behavioral property holds.

negative_fixture_path.description: Path to a script that exits non-zero when the directive's behavioral property is violated.

prohibitions.description: v1.1 (optional). MUST NOT directives synthesised from rejected '## Considered Options' (ADRs only). Each entry MUST have a verifiable source_excerpt pointing to a Cons: bullet or rejected-option body in the parent .md. Extractor never invents a prohibition that is not literally present in rejected-option text (see Phase 2 Rule C in templates/agents/sidecar-extractor.md).

manual_directives.description: User-authored rules preserved across sidecar regenerations. Always included in the effective rule set. Never overwritten by sidecar-extractor.

suppressed_directives.description: Auto-directives the user rejected. Subtracted from directives[] at gov:compile time. Never overwritten by sidecar-extractor.

reminders.description: Pre-action reminders aggregated into governance.md ## Reminders. Format: 'Before {action} → {check} (ref: ID)'. Extracted from ## Confirmation (ADRs) and ## Enforcement (INVs).

oneOf.description: Legacy bare-string form. Verification checklist item in '[ ] {what to check} (ref: ID)' format. Aggregated into governance.md ## Verification Checklist. Human-readable only — no programmatic check.

text.description: Verification checklist item — same content as the bare-string form.

verify.description: Optional shell command that runs the checklist item mechanically. Exit 0 = pass. Used by `bin/edikt verify gov <ID>` to enforce the completion-evidence discipline.

verification.description: Verification checklist items aggregated into governance.md ## Verification Checklist. Two forms accepted (oneOf): bare string (legacy), or {text, verify?} object (preferred for new entries — carries the executable check that proves the item).

migration_preserved.description: v0.6.x two-phase upgrade baseline (Phase A of the migration-as-cleanup refactor). Populated by `edikt migrate sidecars --apply` with the verbatim content of the legacy [edikt:directives:start] block; consumed by the sidecar-extractor agent on the first compile after migration, then stripped from the sidecar by Phase B (compile). Sidecars in steady state do NOT carry this field. Its presence is a structural signal that the artifact has just been migrated and is awaiting its first canonical extraction.

schema_detected.description: What the migrator detected the legacy sentinel block to be. Audit-only; extractor uses the structured content below regardless of detection.

directives.description: Legacy directive strings (the sentinel block's directives:[] list, verbatim). Extractor MUST include each of these in its output, verbatim, then synthesize additional directives from prose that aren't already covered.

manual_directives.description: Legacy manual_directives:[] list, verbatim. Extractor MUST output these in the manual_directives field.

suppressed_directives.description: Legacy suppressed_directives:[] list, verbatim. Extractor MUST output these in the suppressed_directives field.

reminders.description: Legacy reminders:[] list, verbatim. Extractor MUST output these in the reminders field.

verification.description: Legacy verification:[] list, verbatim. Extractor MUST output these in the verification field.

topic.description: Legacy topic if present (v0.5.x sentinels). Extractor MAY use this as a hint when synthesizing the canonical topic field.

signals.description: Legacy signals if present (v0.5.x sentinels). Extractor MAY use this as a hint when synthesizing the canonical signals field.

text.description: The directive sentence as it will appear in compiled governance, ≤ 500 characters. Includes its own ref tail (e.g., '(ref: ADR-NNN)'). 500 chars is deliberate headroom — natural-language rules with multiple clauses routinely run 200–280 chars; rules that would exceed it should be split.

line_start.description: 1-indexed line number in the parent .md where the directive's source text begins.

line_end.description: 1-indexed line number where the source text ends. Must be ≥ line_start. /edikt:doctor verifies this is within the parent file's line count.

quote.description: Verbatim text from the parent .md between line_start and line_end. Used by /edikt:doctor for drift detection (resync triggers when the live quote no longer matches the recorded quote).

verify.description: Optional shell command that returns exit 0 when the directive holds, non-zero when it is violated. Run via `bin/edikt verify gov <ID>`. The completion-evidence discipline refuses to declare success when any verify fails. Omit when no mechanical check is possible — the field stays absent, not empty.

verify_kind.description: v1.2 (optional). The enforcement medium of the verify command. behavioral = runs code and asserts a property; tooling = invokes a stable external tool with a fixed rule ID; structural = grep/file-presence over content (only valid when the directive's property is itself structural, e.g., 'no go.mod at root'). The mechanism-quality axis; layer-independent and harness-independent. Phase B compile enforces: if `verify` is set, `verify_kind` MUST also be set.

intent.description: v1.2 (optional). One-line semantic claim of the directive, generator-neutral. Consumed by the L2 governance-verifier instead of the raw `text`. Must read as the directive's assertion without referencing implementation symbols the generator controls.

falsifying_observation.description: v1.2 (optional). One-line description of what a violation looks like. Used by the L2 verifier to decide PASS/FAIL/NEEDS_REVIEW. Required (non-null) when verify_kind == behavioral; Phase B compile enforces this conditional-required constraint.

human_approved_at.description: v1.2 (optional). RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of human approval. Required by CONTRACT (non-null) for verify_kind == behavioral per ADR-036 §2, but NOT enforced at compile — the check is deferred to SPEC-009 Plan B (AC-4.3), so an unapproved behavioral verify compiles today. Set by `bin/edikt sidecar approve`; the tier-1 wrapper captures the user's decision via Claude Code's AskUserQuestion before dispatching the tier-2 binary.

positive_fixture_path.description: Path to a script that exits 0 when the directive's behavioral property holds.

negative_fixture_path.description: Path to a script that exits non-zero when the directive's behavioral property is violated.

directives.description: Directive list extracted from the parent .md. May be empty (an artifact with no enforceable directives is reported by /edikt:doctor as a warning, not an error). Note: line_end ≥ line_start and line_end ≤ parent_file_line_count are enforced by /edikt:doctor and the compile resync pass — JSON Schema 2020-12 has no standard cross-property comparator. v1.2 conditional-required constraints are declared here but enforced at Phase B compile time rather than at schema-validation time, because JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot express conditional-required across siblings cleanly. Two of the three are enforced today: verify_kind when verify is set, and falsifying_observation when verify_kind == behavioral. The third — human_approved_at when verify_kind == behavioral — is required by contract but NOT checked, its enforcement deliberately deferred to SPEC-009 Plan B (AC-4.3).
